paragraphs: Mentioned in [Yoma 21a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.21a.6). (And it is a place name, as in [Sanhedrin 63b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.63b.9): "Ulla stayed in Kalbeno"; and so explains [Rashi on Zevachim 96a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Zevachim.96a.2.2).)[^1][^2]

notes.text: כא./סג:/צו. give Yoma 21a/Sanhedrin 63b/Zevachim 96a by convention. Hyman identifies Kalbeno as a place-name and נח as stayed/rested, not permanent dwelling or death. The preserved prior Davidson observation reports קלנבו (Kalnevo) and בת (lodged), versus Hyman’s קלבנו/נח; no fresh check of that passage or Rashi is claimed. Both source forms are retained without modern geographic binding. Shemaya’s full רב stays Rav; Ulla has no separate title and Rashi is a commentator label, not title evidence for Shemaya.

The linked passages spell the place Kalnevo. Rashi explains the name by reference to Nevo, and [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3507&lang=en) likewise gives Kalnevo. Hyman’s supplied Kalbeno spelling remains in the translation.
